pos.personaBrief: Benitez's teams were compact, broke quickly and used Torres's pace, with Gerrard at 10 (Bleacher Report, Coaches' Voice); control came from organisation more than ball share.

pro.personaBrief: He wanted direct, quick attacks after regains, built methodically around first and second balls, with safe double-pivot midfielders (Coaches' Voice Coach Watch).

est.personaBrief: Heavily drilled, methodical, zonal shape with defined roles for the pivot, wingers and lone striker (TFT, Coach Watch).

lar.personaBrief: 4-2-3-1 with wingers who worked in both transitions, attacking full-backs and Gerrard central; width was used but the best players were central (Masterclass II).

blo.personaBrief: Pressing game from the front with Torres, pressing higher than any away team at Anfield (LFChistory), yet compact and cautious against skilled opponents.

mar.personaBrief: Defended zonal marking at set pieces for five years and said man marking concedes many goals (Irish Times, The National).

pla.personaBrief: Heavy opposition-specific preparation and per-match tweaks (Milan final plan vs Kaka, Coach Watch) on top of an imposed method.

res.personaBrief: Pragmatic, result-focused manager who rated defensive organisation highest and adjusted to protect results.

sis.personaBrief: System over stars: no luxury players, rotation of big names, everyone has a defined role (TFT, Irish Examiner).

jog.personaBrief: Signed more physical players for the Premier League (Sky 2006), yet valued passing midfielders like Alonso; pivot as reading and organising.

bas.personaBrief: Built through signings from Spain; relied on youngsters only early at Liverpool out of necessity.

lid.personaBrief: Disciplinarian keeping distance from players, banned paella, got rid of those not with him, but had to explain rotation to players.
